transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SA), Lena Ortega (HelioStack - Head of Platform), Ravi Menon (HelioStack - Infra), Claire Dubois (HelioStack - Security), Tomás Rivera (HelioStack - PM)

Summary:
High-level partner discovery: HelioStack is evaluating a partner integration for hybrid deployment (managed control plane + HelioStack-managed GPU pools), wants predictable latency for low-latency chat and batch embedding jobs. Security and VPC/private deployments are primary constraints. Discussed Redwood Dedicated vs Private, routing/fallback, and pilot scope (3-week perf + integration test). Agreed to share spec, perf plan, and security artifacts; tentative pilot start 2026-03-02.

Topics Covered:
- HelioStack infrastructure, current cloud & on-prem mix
- Integration patterns: private control plane, VPC peering, and on-prem connector
- Performance expectations: 90th perc latency targets, throughput for embeddings pipeline
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention
- Commercial: reserved capacity vs shared hosted pricing, revenue share for channel partner

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Liu: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on the partnership side. quick round robin?
[00:07] Lena Ortega: lena here, head of platform at heliostack. we run a mixed fleet, some cloud, some colo.
[00:14] Ravi Menon: ravi, infra lead. mostly GCP + two colo sites with A100-ish hardware.
[00:19] Claire Dubois: claire, security. i'll be looking at compliance and key mgmt.
[00:23] Tomás Rivera: tomás, product. focused on integration points and APIs.
[00:27] Priya Kapoor: priya, solutions eng at redwood. i'll dig into technical constraints, perf, and benchmarks.
[00:33] Marcus Chen: marcus, solutions architect; i'll cover deployment/ops patterns.

[01:05] Jordan Liu: objective for today, align on partner model and pilot scope. we usually run three patterns — hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc — so want to see which maps to your constraints.
[01:18] Lena Ortega: our top constraints: 1) data residency and tenancy for PII-ish payloads, 2) consistent p95 latency under 250ms for our chat frontends, and 3) ability to route to cheapest compatible model if capacity spikes.
[01:32] Priya Kapoor: ok, so sounds like Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you customer-isolated gpu pools with reserved throughput — similar to what you need for predictable p95s. Private gives full control of network and keys but costs more setup.

[02:10] Ravi Menon: can you describe the private option again? our security team will insist on KMS integration, HSM is a maybe, and no egress outside our VPC for certain routes.
[02:21] Priya Kapoor: right, Redwood Private is a customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem packages. we can integrate with your KMS via standard KMIP/KMS connectors or cloud KMS; HSM is supported via partner integrations but that's a separate OKR. For egress restrictions we support VPC peering and private routing, and we can pin model variants so traffic doesn't leave region. note: sometimes the transcription kicks in — sorry i said kvm — i meant k m s —
[02:45] Claire Dubois: (laughs) noted. Also retention windows for logs — we need 1 year of audit logs for any managed control plane activity; is that configurable?
[02:54] Marcus Chen: yes, audit retention is configurable in Redwood Console. you can set per-tenant retention and export to your SIEM via syslog or cloud storage. small caveat: long retention of raw transcripts increases storage costs, we typically recommend token-only audit indexes + redaction.

[04:10] Tomás Rivera: on the perf side, our embedding pipeline is heavy — batch embeddings of 2k vectors every hour and near-real-time chat. how does redwood handle batching/kvcache?
[04:23] Priya Kapoor: we have automatic batching and prefix/KV caching. embeddings pipelines usually benefit from larger batch sizes on dedicated pools — that reduces tokens/sec cost. for chat, KV cache reduces repeated context compute, so p95 latency improves. we'll need a representative workload to size the reserved pools.
[05:00] Ravi Menon: any special kernel/quantization requirements? our colo boxes are old-ish and we might need int8 quant to hit perf on some models.
[05:10] Priya Kapoor: yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles. we support int8-like quant and mixed precision; runtime will pick kernels based on model & hardware. sometimes model names get mangled by the transcript — e.g. i said "r o b o-7b" — i meant the open 7b family.

[06:40] Lena Ortega: commercial question: if we run a channel partnership where HelioStack resells reserved capacity to our customers, how does billing and revenue split work?
[06:52] Jordan Liu: we have partner programs — revenue share or reseller margin models. for reserved capacity (Dedicated) there's a monthly commit; we can set up a partner invoice flow where HelioStack bills end customers and Redwood invoices HelioStack. we'll send the partner gagreement stub — partner-agreement link (shared in chat).

[08:15] Claire Dubois: security deep dive — does redwood have SOC2 type II? how about subprocessor list and pen test reports?
[08:25] Jordan Liu: yes, SOC2 Type II available; we'll share the latest attestation and a subprocessor list. pen-test summary and SSAE stuff can be provided under NDA. also we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and customer-managed encryption keys.

[09:40] Tomás Rivera: routing/fallback: we want automatic fallback to a cheaper model when capacity constrained, but the quality must not degrade below an A/B threshold. is that in the product?
[09:54] Priya Kapoor: yes, smart routing allows policies by latency/cost/quality. you can specify minimum model variants and fallbacks; Redwood Console exposes per-route configs and can do canary rollouts. quality degradation monitoring ties to eval sets so you get alerts if fallback causes regressions.

[12:05] Ravi Menon: what's the network topology for private? do we need a connector in our colo?
[12:15] Marcus Chen: two main patterns: 1) VPC peering + private subnets where redwood agents run in your cloud, 2) on-prem connector (lightweight) that opens only outbound to control plane — we avoid inbound holes. connector can be containerized and runs with restricted privileges.
[13:20] Lena Ortega: the outbound-only connector is appealing. any latency impact?
[13:29] Priya Kapoor: minimal for control plane traffic. inference data path can be kept local if you run the runtime in your environment (private mode). for dedicated in our hosted edge, there's some network hop but we've observed sub-100ms p95 for nearby regions in our benchmarks. we'll verify with your colo site in the pilot.

[15:00] Claire Dubois: keys again — if we supply our own KMS keys, can we rotate without disruption?
[15:08] Marcus Chen: yes we support key rotation with graceful re-encryption; there's a small handoff window but we coordinate rotations. also HSM-backed keys are supported for critical workloads.

[17:30] Tomás Rivera: ok pilot proposal? what would be realistic timeline and scope?
[17:36] Jordan Liu: propose a 3-week pilot: week 0 - integration & network setup, week 1 - perf bench (chat p95 + embeddings throughput), week 2 - resiliency tests and routing fallback validation. deliverables: perf report, security artefacts verified, integration checklist.
[18:00] Ravi Menon: sounds good. any pricing for pilot? free eval for partners?
[18:08] Jordan Liu: we do a funded pilot for qualified partners; costs covered by Redwood for baseline infra usage, HelioStack covers any specialized colo GPU hours if we need exclusive machines. we can agree more in the partner stub.

[20:40] Priya Kapoor: quick tech note: for embedding jobs, we'll instrument token-level cost and give you a per-route cost breakdown in Console so you can decide routing policies for cost vs quality.
[21:00] Lena Ortega: excellent. one more question: multi-tenant segmentation — if we resell to our customers, can they have isolated projects/tenants within the same Dedicated cluster?
[21:12] Marcus Chen: yes, RBAC + project scoping can isolate tenants on the control plane; compute isolation is via dedicated pools or namespaced resources depending on model. we'll document patterns.

[24:20] Claire Dubois: any GDPR/data residency flags for eu customers?
[24:28] Priya Kapoor: region pinning is supported; we can ensure data never leaves EU regions for EU-tenants. export controls for model weights depend on license of the model, we'll check model-specific constraints.

[28:30] Tomás Rivera: regarding the list of candidate GPU vendors, we might prefer CoreWeave or private colo partners. do you have preferred partners?
[28:40] Jordan Liu: we partner with multiple cloud and channel partners, but we try to keep the platform vendor-agnostic. we do have reference configs for CoreWeave, Equinox, and some colo integrators. we'll include a partner compatibility matrix.

[33:50] Ravi Menon: operational question — how are upgrades handled? we run strict maintenance windows.
[34:00] Marcus Chen: upgrade paths: we do canary deploys by default and have scheduled maintenance windows per-customer. for Private deployments, you control the upgrade cadence if you run the control plane on-prem.

[40:10] Priya Kapoor: quick demo note — if useful, we can schedule a short screen-share to walk through Console to show per-route dashboards and the rollout UI.
[40:20] Lena Ortega: yes please, let's do that as a follow-up; product team wants UI walkthrough.

[44:00] Jordan Liu: recap: we'll send partner stub, security docs, and perf plan. HelioStack shares infra diagram and SOC contacts. aim to start pilot 2026-03-02.

[44:40] Tomás Rivera: any blockers from our side? Claire?
[44:45] Claire Dubois: need to review SOC2 & pen test; if all good, security sign-off not blocking.

[45:00] Jordan Liu: perfect. i'll put the stub in the chat and email. thanks everyone.

[55:10] End of meeting.

Notes / references shared in chat: partner-integration-spec.pdf (link), security-attachments.zip (link), proposed-pilot-plan.xlsx (link)
